source_snapshot.title: P.-C. Alombert and J. Colin, La campagne de 1805 en Allemagne, tome II (third part, Du Rhin au Danube)
source_snapshot.author: P.-C. Alombert and J. Colin (Section historique de l'État-major de l'armée)
source_snapshot.edition: Paris: Librairie militaire R. Chapelot et Cie, 1902 (year printed on the title page in the OCR); tome II ('Troisième partie, Du Rhin au Danube'), Princeton University copy digitised by Google; Internet Archive OCR (Tesseract 5.0). Not checked against print.
source_snapshot.archival_identifier: Internet Archive alombert-la-campagne-de-1805-en-allemagne-v-2; Princeton University copy, digitised by Google
source_snapshot.document_date_note: A French General Staff narrative printing documents of August to October 1805. The registered pages are returns headed 'au passage du Rhin dans les premiers jours de vendémiaire an XIV' (vendémiaire an XIV began on 23 September 1805), with no day given, so no document date is recorded; the print year is not an event date.
source_snapshot.dependency_note: Official history of the French army's Section historique (published 'sous la direction de la Section historique de l'etat-major de l'armee'), by P.-C. Alombert (contrôleur de l'administration de l'armée) and J. Colin (chef d'escadron d'artillerie), printed 1902-1908; not a record of 1805 itself. It narrates and prints French orders, letters, reports and divisional journals of the campaign, so it is the French side's own record; it cites the Correspondance de Napoleon Ier by number and shares the headquarters papers of Napoleon and the marshals' reports, so it is not independent of them. Austrian-side statements are second-hand, from French documents and from Austrian publications it cites (for example Schonhals, Der Krieg 1805, Vienne 1873, in a footnote of the introduction). Krauss (1912) names this work as a basis of his account of the French side (his preface), so Krauss is not independent of it for French orders and movements.
source_snapshot.rights: Published 1902-1908; Internet Archive marks the item with the Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0. Full OCR text retained; page images, where registered, are downscaled single pages.
source_snapshot.inspection: Retained complete parent. Located the corps returns 'au passage du Rhin' of chapter II by keyword search and read only the registered page images of pp. 162, 163, 165 and 166 (the 5th corps, the 6th corps and the cavalry reserve); the OCR of these tables is garbled and was not used, and the rest of the volume was not read.

passages.quote:
Monsieur le Maréclal-Ministre, j'ai Lruuvé à Strasbourg, où je 
suis arrivé hier, les ordres de Sa Majesté et les instructions que 
vous m'avez fait l'honneur de m'y adresser. Les intentions de 
l'Empereur etles vôtres seront remplies ; je vais reconnaître moi- 
même les cantonnements destinés à la cavalerie, et m'assurer 
qu'on y a fait les approvisionnements de fourrages nécessaires.
passages.locator: Pinned tome-II OCR, lines 18369-18374, document context c01; printed page/date not image-verified.
passages.interpretation_en: Murat reports finding imperial orders and Berthier instructions on his arrival at Strasbourg and proposes to inspect cavalry cantonments and forage provision.
passages.scope_limit: Reported receipt is positive evidence, but the received documents are not identified here as an original general-command instrument; arrival, document and effective appointment times are not synchronized.

passages.locator: Alombert and Colin, tome II, murat-berthier-letter; pinned OCR lines 18376–18378; character range [419656, 419839); running-page digits not image-verified
passages.interpretation_en: Murat reports being nominated lieutenant to command the Grande Armée in the Emperor's absence.
passages.scope_limit: A self-reported nomination and absence condition do not establish an effective initial date, full mandate or exact transfer/end. Read with m003 and m009.

passages.quote:

passages.locator: Pinned tome-II OCR, lines 23720-23727, document context c04; printed page/date not image-verified.
passages.interpretation_en: The Emperor sets conditions for Lannes' position and leaves Murat to coordinate with Lannes against a small opposing force at the Kniebis while restricting a serious engagement there.
passages.scope_limit: Limited discretion within stated conditions, not authority over every corps or permission for an unrestricted battle. No hypothetical condition is coded as an observed event.

passages.quote:

seront réunies, mon inteution étant que ces troupes soient

passages.locator: Pinned tome-II OCR, lines 23729-23736, document context c04; printed page/date not image-verified.
passages.interpretation_en: The Emperor requests information on the assembling Würtemberg troops, states his intention that they be immediately under Murat's orders, and gives a conditional advance instruction.
passages.scope_limit: A prospective/conditional operational attachment is retained as such. Actual assembly, effective subordination, persistent unit identity and local people are unestablished.

passages.scope_limit: Positive reported cross-corps coordination under a specific contingency, not unrestricted general authority or proof the delay occurred. Dates and execution remain unselected.

passages.quote:

quelque sorte, d'autorité centrale, Cependant, je prie Votre Ma- 












jesté d'être parfaitement rassurée, car, si vous u'arriviez aujour- 
d'hui, je n'oublierais pas que j'ai l'honneur d'être votre lieutenant

passages.locator: Pinned tome-II OCR, lines 32434-32456, document context c06; printed page/date not image-verified.
passages.interpretation_en: Murat reports direct ministerial crossing orders to the marshals and to himself as cavalry-reserve commander rather than army commander in the Emperor's absence. He worries about decentralized action but asserts that, if the Emperor does not arrive that day, he will act as lieutenant and expects compliance.
passages.scope_limit: This undated self-report distinguishes command scopes and claims expected authority; it is not a superior confirmation, proof of actual obedience, an effective revocation or a dated handover. Its placement does not supply its missing date.

passages.locator: Pinned tome-II OCR, lines 35209-35223, document context c07; printed page/date not image-verified.
passages.interpretation_en: Berthier conveys the Emperor's instructions: Murat is to tell Baraguey-d'Hilliers to protect the park if needed and supply a guard battalion under the park director during the movement; Murat is to move headquarters to Rastatt, remain until the park has passed that position, personally see its passage and report.
passages.scope_limit: Prescribed protection/guard arrangements, hierarchy and a task-specific stop condition are supported. The guard is placed under the park director during movement. Actual assumption, passage, reporting and completion times are unestablished; this is not an endpoint for all Murat authority or a local people total.

authority_observations.disposition: Retain nomination/claimed absence role with its own general-scope question and later undated qualification; no blanket selection over the entire Grande Armée.
Positive bounded task authority under imperial direction; crossing decision expressly retained by superior.
Limited coordination with Lannes and reported contingent delay authority for named corps, not an equality with overall army command.
Imperial intention about Würtemberg troops; actual attachment and local population not established.
Prescribed protection arrangement, location/duration and report, with guard authority under the park director during movement. Actual coverage/execution unestablished.
Retain superior command/presence, distinguish it from a proven end of all Murat delegation.
Explicit mission under superior direction, preserved separately from the earlier absence/general-command candidate; continuity or effective transition between mandates not selected.

assessment.superior_authority_retained: Emperor's superior operational/policy authority; replacing Murat would not replace the Emperor. Retaining that authority is not an assumption that every later imperial response is fixed regardless of the delegate's choices.
assessment.reason: The new unit supports positive task/authority observations and prescribed relative conditions, but not a continuous unrestricted general-command mandate or an effective interval. No analytical boundary convention is selected here. Local role retention does not require global IDs/full tenure; a future comparison must declare its task/force scope and window rather than pool all these observations as one appointment.
